paper.title: A Contribution to the Mathematical Theory of Epidemics
paper.authors: W. O. Kermack, A. G. McKendrick
paper.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 115

redacted_excerpt: The paper introduces the compartmental S-I-R model of epidemic spread: dS/dt = -beta*S*I/N, dI/dt = beta*S*I/N - gamma*I, dR/dt = gamma*I, where S, I, R are the susceptible, infected, and recovered populations and N = S + I + R is constant. An epidemic occurs when the basic reproduction number R0 = beta/gamma exceeds 1: the infected fraction rises to a single peak and then declines, and the epidemic terminates with a nonzero fraction of the population never infected. As a validation, the paper fits the model to weekly deaths from the plague epidemic in Bombay (1905-06). For this replication, integrate the ODE system numerically (e.g., RK4 or scipy's solve_ivp) with N = 1000, I(0) = 1, R(0) = 0, beta = 0.4 per day, gamma = 0.1 per day (R0 = 4), over 100 days.
figure_caption: Time evolution of the S-I-R epidemic model over 100 days (beta = 0.4, gamma = 0.1, N = 1000, I0 = 1): three curves showing susceptible, infected, and recovered populations, with the infected curve rising to a single epidemic peak and declining, and a labeled legend.
claim: When R0 = beta/gamma > 1, the deterministic SIR model produces a single-peaked epidemic that terminates before the susceptible population is exhausted.
